text:
sam: quick sync — sketched a lightweight pattern for handling degraded variants without full canary rollbacks. idea: a proxy-relay that accepts a degeneration signal and strips nonessential state (prefix cache, large kv blobs) to recover throughput, with automatic fallback to previous variant if error/sla break. link: go/deg-proxy-rfc :thinking:

marta: can you paste the routing decision? curious how this interacts with session affinity and cache warmup.

sam: yep, minimal sketch below — decision is local to the router, driven by a deg signal we propagate on the request path. session affinity preserved by pinning session -> original backend, proxy-relay only used as a fast-path for stateless requests. snippet:

```
# header example
X-Deg-Signal: level=2;probe=rt;origin=observer

# routing pseudocode
if header.level >= 2 and request.is_stateless():
  route_to(proxy-relay)
else:
  route_to(regular-backend)
```

raj: couple tradeoffs: 1) proxy-relay reduces tail but adds another box to maintain (ops cost). 2) stripping state may change outputs for some prompts (reranking/recall). need a quality gate.

lee: agree on quality gate. suggest we attach a lightweight checksum of prefix length and a sample hash to telemetry so we can detect semantic drift fast. e.g. send sample_id + prefix_len in tracing span.

sam: good. for fallback triggers, propose combining 3 signals: (1) spike in latency/error, (2) quality regression on sampled prompts, (3) observer flag from rollout controller. any two-of-three triggers automatic rollback.

marta: how do we test this in Dedicated vs Private? customers will have KV-caches on-prem. we can't strip their caches remotely.

sam: for Private, the proxy-relay would run inside the customer VPC as an optional sidecar. the deg-signal is purely control-plane-originated and honored locally. ops impact: packaging sidecar + small lifecycle hooks.

raj: one more: telemetry cardinality. if we start emitting sample hashes per-request we explode metrics. suggest sampling 0.1% and have aggregated counters for drift buckets.

lee: implementation note: keep the deg-signal as an opaque header so non-redwood components ignore it. also add an acknowledgement header from proxy-relay: `X-Deg-Handled: true;mode=strip` so request traces show the path.

ops-bot: deploy triggered: rollout/dg-proxy-relay/patch-1 -> staging (sha: abcd123). :rocket:

marta: can we add a small cookbook for operators? steps: enable deg-signal, set thresholds, enable sample telemetry, run warmup job. if staging looks good, promote.

sam: I'll write the follow-up RFC section with operator checklist and the two-of-three fallback rule. will include example config: 

```yaml
deg_policy:
  sampling_pct: 0.1
  thresholds:
    latency_ms: 500
    error_rate_pct: 1.5
  fallback_condition: at_least_two
```

lee: propose we add a canary experiment: mirror 10% traffic to proxy-relay path (no strip) to validate equivalence before enabling strip-mode.

sam: love that. i'll update the doc and open a tiny test PR for the mirror-only experiment. tagging @marta and @raj for review. :thumbsup:
